items.followUp: Define density and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Pressure is defined as force acting per unit area.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is force per unit area.

rubric.why: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, equivalent to a newton per square metre.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pascal (Pa) or N/m².

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area of a surface.
The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

items.followUp: Define longitudinal strain and write its formula.

rubric.why: Strain is the ratio of a change in dimension to the original dimension.
rubric.description: Defines strain as a ratio of dimensional change to original dimension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the general definition or an equivalent formula.

rubric.why: Tensile strain is the extension per original length caused by a tensile force.
rubric.description: Distinguishes tensile strain as the increase in length relative to original length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition or an equivalent explanation.

modelAnswer: Strain is the ratio of the change in a body's dimension to its original dimension.
Tensile strain is the increase in length (extension) per unit original length when a tensile force acts on the body.

items.followUp: State two ways friction can be increased and two ways it can be reduced.

rubric.why: Smoothing or polishing reduces surface irregularities and friction.
rubric.description: States that surfaces can be made smooth or polished.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for smoothing or polishing the surfaces.

rubric.why: A lubricant separates surfaces and reduces friction.
rubric.description: States that a lubricant can be applied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for lubrication using oil, grease, or another lubricant.

rubric.why: Ball bearings or rollers replace sliding friction with smaller rolling friction.
rubric.description: States that ball bearings or rollers can be used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using ball bearings, rollers, or another rolling method.

rubric.why: Streamlining reduces frictional resistance from air or water.
rubric.description: States that bodies can be streamlined to reduce fluid friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for streamlining.

modelAnswer: Polish or smooth the surfaces in contact.
Apply a lubricant, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces.
Use ball bearings or rollers to replace sliding friction with rolling friction.
Streamline bodies moving through air or water.

items.followUp: A force of 20 N makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing a force by components that have the same combined effect as the original force.
rubric.description: Defines resolution of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a force is split into components whose resultant is the original force.

rubric.why: The resolved components are at right angles to one another.
rubric.description: States that the components are perpendicular.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the components as mutually perpendicular.

rubric.why: For an angle θ measured from the horizontal, the horizontal component is F cos θ.
rubric.description: Gives the horizontal component relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fx = F cos θ or an equivalent statement.

rubric.why: For an angle θ measured from the horizontal, the vertical component is F sin θ.
rubric.description: Gives the vertical component relation and method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fy = F sin θ or an equivalent statement.

modelAnswer: Resolution of a force is the process of replacing a force by two or more component forces that have the same effect as the original force.
To resolve a force into perpendicular components, take its projections along two mutually perpendicular axes.
If a force F makes an angle θ with the horizontal axis, its horizontal component is Fx = F cos θ.
Its vertical component is Fy = F sin θ; the vector sum of these perpendicular components is the original force.

items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power in watts and horsepower. Take g = 9.8 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W.

rubric.why: The calculation must use the given mass, height, and time in SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, and t = 10 s.

rubric.why: Power is work done per unit time, and the work in lifting the water is mgh.
rubric.description: Selects the correct power formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P = W/t = mgh/t.

rubric.why: Substitution of the data gives the power in watts.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given data into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution, allowing g = 9.8 or 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Using g = 9.8 gives 1097.6 W; using the approximation g = 10 gives 1120 W.
rubric.description: Calculates power in watts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1097.6 W (or approximately 1.10 × 10³ W) or 1120 W when g = 10 m/s² is used.

rubric.why: Converting watts to horsepower gives approximately 1.47 hp, or about 1.5 hp.
rubric.description: Converts the power to horsepower.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct horsepower conversion using 1 hp = 746 W.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, t = 10 s, and g = 9.8 m/s².
Power, P = work done / time = mgh/t.
Since 1 hp = 746 W, power in horsepower = 1097.6 W / 746 W per hp.
Power = 1.47 hp (approximately).

items.followUp: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. Find its least count.

rubric.why: Least count is found by dividing the pitch by the number of divisions on the circular scale.
rubric.description: Writes the least-count formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for least count = pitch / number of circular-scale divisions.

rubric.why: The standard least count of the screw gauge is 0.01 mm, equivalent to 0.001 cm.
rubric.description: Gives the least-count value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0.01 mm or its equivalent.

modelAnswer: Least count of a screw gauge = pitch of screw / number of divisions on the circular scale.
Its value is 0.01 mm (or 0.001 cm).

items.followUp: Convert 90 km h⁻¹ into m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: To convert km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹, multiply by 1000/3600, or 5/18.
rubric.description: Uses the correct conversion factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for applying the km/h to m/s conversion factor.

rubric.why: 70 × 1000/3600 = 19.44 m/s approximately.
rubric.description: Gives the converted speed with an SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 19.44 m/s.

modelAnswer: Given speed = 70 km h⁻¹.
Speed in SI units = 70 × (1000 m / 3600 s).
Speed = 19.44 m s⁻¹ (approximately).

items.followUp: Define force and state whether it is a scalar or vector quantity.

rubric.why: Momentum is defined as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating p = mv or the equivalent definition.

rubric.why: Momentum has both magnitude and direction because it depends on velocity.
rubric.description: Classifies momentum as a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that momentum is a vector.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Momentum is a vector quantity.
